commit.author: Timo Sulg <timgluz@gmail.com>

lines.content: - Verified via Playwright + screenshot: `/blog/` renders correctly with the topbar Blog link present and the empty-state message, zero console errors.

- `npx astro check` (0 errors), `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean), `npx vitest run` (208 tests), `npm run build:check` (still-live Vite pipeline, unaffected — `Topbar.astro` isn't in its dependency graph) all pass.

- Next: Phase 8 (testing) — update `vitest.config.ts`/`playwright.config.ts` for Astro's dev server (default port 4321 vs Vite's 5173), run the full Playwright suite (`tests/webmcp.spec.ts`) against the Astro build, manual Lighthouse/CLS check on the homepage.
- `vitest.config.ts`: already standalone and confirmed working since Phase 1, nothing further needed.

- `playwright.config.ts`: **deliberately did NOT edit yet** — its `baseURL`/`webServer.command` (`npm run dev`, port 5173) still point at the still-live Vite pipeline per the Phase 1/3/6 deferral pattern. Instead, verified compatibility directly: started `astro dev --port 5173` manually (matching the config's expected URL exactly, no file edits) and ran the full suite — Playwright's `reuseExistingServer` (default true outside CI) detected the already-running server and used it instead of invoking `npm run dev`. **All 10 subtests passed** (`tests/webmcp.spec.ts`'s 5 tests × 2 browser projects: chrome, chromium) with zero test changes — the WebMCP form markup and worker wiring ported byte-for-byte, so the existing suite Just Works against Astro. Actual `playwright.config.ts` edit (pointing `webServer.command` at `astro dev`) deferred to Phase 9/10 alongside the `npm run dev` script flip.

- CLS check: built production output, served via `astro preview`, measured Cumulative Layout Shift with a `PerformanceObserver` (`layout-shift` entries, `buffered: true`) across 4 representative page types (home, a doc page, an explainer page, the blog index). **Result: 0.0000 on all four** — no regression toward the prior 0.67 incident. Confirms the plan's expectation that Astro's default `<head>`-hoisted CSS (no client-side CSS injection anywhere in this migration) structurally avoids the exact anti-pattern that caused that incident.

- Next: Phase 9 (CI/CD) — update `package.json` scripts to flip `dev`/`build`/`build:check`/`preview` from Vite to Astro, add `astro check` to `.github/workflows/teeline-web.yml`, update `playwright.config.ts`'s `webServer`/`baseURL` to match. This is also where `vite.config.ts` finally gets deleted (deferred since Phase 1) and the old `*-page.ts` mount scripts + `algorithms/<id>/{index,explainer/index}.html` shells get removed (deferred since Phase 6) — Phase 9 and Phase 10 (cutover) are tightly coupled; may end up doing both in one pass.

commit.message:
Log Phase 8 (testing) completion for Astro migration

Verified compatibility without editing playwright.config.ts yet
(still points at the live Vite pipeline per the established deferral
pattern) — started astro dev manually on the expected port, all 10
WebMCP Playwright subtests passed unchanged. CLS measured at 0.0000
across 4 page types via PerformanceObserver on a production build,
confirming no regression toward the prior 0.67 incident.

Implements [[tasks/teeline-web-astro7-migration]]
